summaries.Good news: North America's largest wildlife overpass is preventing animal collisions at a stunning 91% rate, while innovative agricultural textiles are tripling strawberry yields and reducing pesticide use—real solutions creating tangible progress for nature and food systems.
summaries.Ideas: Breakthrough medical implants are restoring sight to macular degeneration patients, while research reveals remote work correlates with higher birth rates and Gen Z is deliberately choosing physical experiences over digital ones—signaling meaningful shifts in how we live and what we value.
summaries.Technology: Apple is launching its first smart home devices after over a decade, Tesla's Roadster can briefly leave the ground using SpaceX thrusters, and Nvidia's new RTX Spark processor is rivaling Apple's chip performance—marking major platform moves and hardware leaps.
summaries.Design: A Bangladesh rug factory won architecture's top international prize for dismantling workplace hierarchies through design, while architects continue exploring adaptive reuse (a 1908 prison becoming luxury hotel) and furniture collections extending studio practice into new territories.

items.title: North America’s Largest Wildlife Overpass Is Working: Animal Collisions on I-25 Down 91%
items.snippet: In March, GNN reported that North America’s largest wildlife overpass had opened in December over Interstate 25 near Larkspur, in Colorado. Now, 10 months on from its opening, data has demonstrated that the 6-lane lifeline for bears, elk, moose, and other animals is working, with 91% fewer collision
items.line: A 91% reduction in animal collisions proves thoughtful infrastructure design can coexist with wildlife—real lives saved through elegant engineering.
